newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher for fifth straight session on Wednesday due to active U.S. dollar sales by local commercial banks amid the banking system's liquidity squeeze, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.858, sliding from an intra-day high of T$27.854 but higher than Tuesday's T$27.885 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$337 million.

Dealers said persistently tight liquidity and the central bank's apparent determination to stabilise the currency on the eve of Hong Kong's handover, a politically delicate moment for Taiwan, had checked the unit's months-long depreciation trend.
"Local banks were active U.S. sellers in the market," said one dealer.
"It is difficult to say whether the tight liquidity or the central bank is the dominant factor for the Taiwan dollar's rebound. It's probably a combination of both," the dealer said.
The surging Taiwan interbank rate has prompted investors to sell U.S. dollars in exchange for Taiwan dollars.

Taiwan's interbank rate roared briefly above nine percent and closed at a 21-month peak on Tuesday despite central bank stabilisation efforts, as a frantic stock market siphoned funds from the banking system.
At 0800 GMT, the overnight rate was at 8.493 percent.
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar's downside was limited in the run-up to Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule.

"A depreciation of the local currency likely would give other people an impression of a lack of confidence," the dealer said. "The central bank will do whatever it can to prevent this from happening."
A stable range of T$27.85-90 was seen for Wednesday.
